related_work: The Bauhaus started in Germany in 1919. It said art, design and technology are really one thing. Ryan also showed two works. Extinction Gong hits a gong every time an animal species dies out, which happens about every 19 minutes. Rare Earthenware uses toxic mud from a rare earth mine to make three vases. Their sizes show how much waste is made for a phone, a laptop and a car battery.
conclusion_future_work: This class showed me that art can use data to make people think about big problems, like climate and extinction. Next, I need to check Blackboard for the reading about climate and migration. Next week, we will keep talking about planetary design, and a guest will talk about art and technology in South America.
results_discussion: I learned that speculative design doesn’t try to find the final answer. It asks questions and helps people imagine the future. Ryan said design solves problems, but art shows problems. Bobby showed that the same satellite can make two very different pictures of Earth: the “Blue Marble” makes us feel the Earth is weak, and the night-light “Black Marble” makes us think about globalisation. He writes all his own software from a blank page. He also said we shouldn’t let AI write our code. We can use it like a teacher to explain errors. This is very useful advice for me.
title: week8
introduction: In the afternoon, Ryan talked about the Bauhaus and speculative design. In the second half, our guest, Bobby Pietrusko from the University of Pennsylvania, talked online about four of his projects. They were about how satellites and data shape the way we see the whole Earth.
